markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small, testable SASRec extension. All improvements below are hypotheses; the supplied diagnostics establish neither validation gains nor functional compatibility.

### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) SASRec already provides causal sequence features. A residual extension preserves this useful starting representation. (2) Users report that broad associations displace recent intent. Explicit recent-history features could strengthen evidence for choosing an item now. (3) Repeated narrow preferences are useful, whereas isolated interactions are ambiguous. Retrieving historical evidence with recent intent could distinguish these cases without inventing user traits.

**Related-work insights.** (1) [Hierarchical long/short-term modeling](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) retrieves persistent interests using recent intent. This motivates lightweight attention over historical items. (2) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) motivates learning against multiple negatives. Electronics’ 14.95% wrong-ranking rate makes separation a reasonable experimental target. (3) [MQSA-TED](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01056) models item transitions. Directional evidence could help distinguish plausible continuation from generic similarity, although transitions cannot establish equipment compatibility.

These insights define three directions: temporal evidence selection, ranking objectives, and directional transitions.

### Framework and candidate assessment

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment lists a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea and mechanism | Scores | Critical assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **Intent-gated SASRec:** fuse recent and retrieved historical evidence; train with 32 uniform negatives | 5/8/8/8/4 | Originality: + targeted combination, − established components. Potential: + extensible, − gate may collapse. User: + recent intent and repeated preferences, − cannot verify compatibility. Model: + targets weak separation, − margins may not generalize. Difficulty: + small modules, − causal masking requires care. |
| **Objective-only:** retain SASRec; replace BCE with multi-negative sampled softmax | 2/7/4/9/2 | Originality: + clean adaptation, − standard objective. Potential: + strong baseline, − limited expressiveness. User: + sharper ranking, − no explicit intent mechanism. Model: + more comparisons, − false negatives. Difficulty: + simple, − memory grows. |
| **Transition residual:** add smoothed directed training-transition scores | 4/6/7/5/3 | Originality: + useful integration, − established graphs. Potential: + interpretable, − sparse coverage. User: + plausible continuation, − transitions imply no utility guarantee. Model: + extra evidence, − weak tail support. Difficulty: + sparse counts, − smoothing requires tuning. |

### Selected idea: intent-gated SASRec

Select the first idea for early-stage feasibility. It explicitly targets two user failures: broad associations outranking recent intent, and isolated interactions outweighing repeated narrow preferences. Multi-negative training targets Electronics’ weak positive–negative separation.

At each causal prefix, compute recent mean embedding `r`, historical attention `s = Attention(query=r, keys=prefix_items)`, and gate `g = sigmoid(MLP(r,s))`. Score with `f = LayerNorm(h_SASRec + g*W_r*r + (1-g)*W_s*s)` and shared item embeddings. Optimize sampled softmax against 32 distinct uniform negatives, excluding padding, positives and observed training-history items.

Compare baseline, objective-only and gated variants using unchanged macro validation HR@10. Preserve four-category routing, seeds, `GAGC_DATA_DIR`, trial-local artifacts and the predictor writer. Keep diagnosis methods architecture-compatible; track margins without treating them as validation performance.

idea.description: Add a causal recent-intent and historical-evidence gate to SASRec, trained with uniform multi-negative sampled softmax.
idea.motivation: Address broad relevance outranking recent intent and isolated interactions outweighing repeated specific preferences. Target the observed weak positive–negative separation, especially in Electronics, without assuming unavailable compatibility attributes.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only training histories and existing item embeddings. Start with a five-item recent window and 32 negatives as experimental settings, not established optima. Mask padding and future positions in all pooling operations; handle empty prefixes safely. Sample distinct negatives excluding the positive and observed training-history items, reducing the count when necessary. Retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four category models and routing, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Save new modules and configuration beneath the trial directory and update the predictor writer to reconstruct them. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions; expose the actual model through view.model and the fused features through log2feats. Report unavailable category breakdowns as unavailable. Select solely using the pinned macro validation HR@10; neither baseline executable source nor a verified integration interface was supplied, so this is implementation pseudocode rather than a runnable replacement.
idea.pseudocode:
for each category, with training seed 42:
    initialize baseline SASRec and gate/projection modules
    for each training batch:
        h = SASRec(sequence)
        for every valid causal position t:
            prefix = nonpadding sequence[:t+1]
            r = mean(item_emb(prefix[-5:]))
            s = attention(query=r, keys=item_emb(prefix), values=item_emb(prefix))
            g = sigmoid(MLP(concat(r, s)))
            f[t] = LayerNorm(h[t] + g * Wr(r) + (1-g) * Ws(s))
            negatives = distinct_uniform_items_excluding_training_history_and_positive()
            logits = dot(f[t], item_emb([positive[t]] + negatives))
        loss = mean(cross_entropy(logits, target=0) over valid positions)
        update_parameters(loss)
    retain checkpoint using permitted validation protocol
write predictor with identical fusion, embeddings, configuration and category routing
compare baseline, objective-only and gated variants by macro validation HR@10

originality.positive: Combines intent-conditioned historical retrieval with a compact SASRec residual tailored to the reported failures.
originality.negative: Attention pooling, gating and multi-negative objectives are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Provides a small platform for studying when recent intent should retrieve sustained preferences.
future_potential.negative: The gate may become constant, and observed interactions cannot establish practical compatibility or satisfied needs.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the SASRec encoder and shared item embeddings with a few additional modules.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal pooling, efficient negative sampling, diagnostic adaptation and matching predictor serialization require careful integration.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention sequence encoder and shared item scoring baseline.
limitations: The supplied baseline diagnostics show weak separation in some categories and user complaints about broad relevance.

related_work.title: Hierarchical long/short-term modeling (2025)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes recent-intent retrieval over multiple historical interests.
limitations: Its reported design does not establish gains on the pinned RecHarness benchmark.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates multiple negatives and generalized BCE to address sampling-induced overconfidence.
limitations: The proposed sampled-softmax objective is an alternative experiment, not the gSASRec objective.
More negatives increase computation and can include plausible unobserved positives.

related_work.title: MQSA-TED
contributions: Combines short/long attention queries with distillation of global item transitions.
limitations: Observed transitions do not establish functional complementarity or equipment compatibility.
